I hope so, but beyond test scores, I want to protect more than a quiet classroom. I want time to meet a point of view different from mine through words. I look over the lesson plan on the teacher's desk. I don't want us to spend less time with the texts just to check if phones are put away.

In my notebook's margin, I write what I want to tell the school. Before it is decided to lock devices away, I want room to think about it, too. I don't want to put my responsibility for managing my own device use into the back.

last_attempts_log.asr_text: Everyone wants to value the time they spend learning. I think we agree on that. But when a decision is wrong, people lose different things. They also have to carry different amounts themselves, so we do not all use the same standard to decide if it was a good choice. The power to decide where money goes, run a classroom, and manage your own life are not the same. Even if you have little say in a decision, its weight may not be any lighter. Even if you have something very important to protect, you may not get a say in the decision, whose understanding is still waiting to be put into words.
